title: Psilocybin-Assisted Physical Therapy in Chronic Low Back Pain
official: Psilocybin in Chronic Low Back Pain: An Integrative Study of Lab-Based Mechanisms and Real-World Physical Therapy Outcomes
summary: The purpose of this research study is to investigate whether a single administration of psilocybin can improve interoceptive awareness (awareness of bodily sensations) in individuals with chronic low back pain undergoing physical therapy, and whether these improvements are linked to pain relief and better physical therapy outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 1\. Ability to provide informed consent in English.
* 2\. Provision of signed and dated informed consent form.
* 3\. Stated willingness to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study.
* 4\. Male and female participants aged 21-65 years.
* 5\. CLBP, uniformly defined as high-impact or bothersome non-cancer low back pain lasting ≥ three months that occurs most days and limits life or work activities.
* 6\. At least moderate pain-related disability as measured by a total score on the ODI ≥ 15.
* 7\. For women of childbearing potential, must have a negative urine pregnancy test at screening and immediately before dose administration.

  o Use of one highly effective contraception (e.g., IUD, barrier method) for ≥ 1 month prior to screening.
* 8\. Participants are required to commit to employing dual contraceptive methods throughout the study and to abstain from sperm or egg donation during the study period and for 28 days following the final drug dose for ova, and for 90 days following the final drug dose for sperm. Dual contraceptive methods encompass the use of a barrier contraceptive, such as condoms, coupled with another effective method capable of preventing pregnancy, such as oral or parenteral contraceptives, intrauterine devices, spermicide, and the like.
* 9\. Resting blood pressure ≤ 135/85 mmHg (average of three screenings) and resting heart rate 60-100 bpm.
* 10\. Normal screening EKG: QTcF \< 450 ms; no clinically significant arrhythmias, ischemia, or bundle branch block.
* 11\. Hepatic and renal function within acceptable limits: AST/ALT ≤ 2× ULN; bilirubin ≤ 1.5× ULN; eGFR ≥ 50 mL/min/1.73 m².
* 12\. Ability to safely ingest oral capsules for the dosing visit.
* 13\. Safe transportation plan after the dosing session (e.g., designated driver).
* 14\. Signed medical release permitting the study team to communicate with outside providers for medication/therapy history or crisis management.
* 15\. Designation of an adult emergency contact (relative, spouse, close friend) willing to monitor for mood/behavior changes post-dose and provide transportation if needed.
* 16\. Access to a personal mobile device that can access the internet.
* 17\. Agreement to attend preparatory and integration sessions, follow-up visits, and to respond to telephone/email contacts.

Exclusion Criteria:

* 1\. Hallucinogen Use Disorder or Hallucinogen Persisting Perceptual Disorder.
* 2\. History of intolerance to drugs known to significantly alter perception e.g., psilocybin, LSD, salvinorin A, mescaline, etc.
* 3\. Personal or first-degree family history of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder with psychotic features; any history of substance-induced psychosis or current psychotic symptoms. Personal symptoms will be evaluated during screening using the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale 88, family history will be evaluated during the clinical interview.
* 4\. Active suicidal ideation or behavior in the past 3 months, as indicated on the C-SSRS.
* 5\. Use of classic psychedelics (5-HT2A agonists) within the preceding 12 months.
* 6\. Unwillingness to abstain from the use of psychedelics, THC, and other substances for at least 7 days pre-dose through 4 weeks post-dose. THC abstinence will be confirmed via point-of-care urine 11-nor-9-carboxy-THC testing with a cut-off ≤ 50 ng/mL87,88.
* 7\. Current moderate or severe depression, as indicated by a score of ≥ 3 on the depression subscale (items 1 and 2) of the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4).
* 8\. Total score on the ODI ≥ 35, indicating an individual is "completely disabled."
* 9\. Meeting DSM-5 criteria for alcohol or substance use disorders (other than tobacco use disorder) within the last year.
* 10\. Clinically significant medical disorders (e.g., moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment \[Child-Pugh B/C\], AST/ALT \> 2× ULN, bilirubin \> 1.5× ULN, eGFR \< 50 mL/min/1.73 m², diabetes, uncontrolled thyroid disease).
* 11\. Known or suspected cardiovascular disease, including but not limited to atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, history of myocardial infarction, structural heart disease, congestive heart failure, and/or uncontrolled hypertension. Participants whose hypertension is controlled (i.e., on a stable medication regimen) may still be eligible provided their screening blood pressure meets the threshold criterion.
* 12\. Neurological conditions altering nociceptive response (e.g., stroke, neuropathy) or history of seizure/head injury with \> 30 minutes loss of consciousness.
* 13\. Contraindications to nociceptive testing (e.g., Raynaud Syndrome, untreated hypertension \> 135/85 mmHg).
* 14\. Current use of serotonergic medications (e.g., SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs).
* 15\. Current regular use of medications affecting pain (e.g., opioids, gabapentinoids, cyclobenzaprine).
* 16\. Current regular use of inhibitors of UGT1A9, UGT1A10, MAO and aldehyde or alcohol dehydrogenase.
* 17\. Current regular use of 5-hydroxytryptophan, L-tryptophan, and/or St. John's wort.
* 18\. Any cognitive deficit impairing consent/participation.
* 19\. Major neurocognitive disorders (e.g., dementia, delirium, amnestic).
* 20\. Abnormal EKG findings (e.g., ischemia, infarct patterns, bundle branch block, atrial fibrillation, QTcF ≥ 450 ms).
* 21\. Resting QTcF prolongation or other torsades de pointes risk factors (e.g. uncontrolled electrolyte disturbances, family history of sudden death, torsadogenic medications).
* 22\. Any other condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would compromise safety or ability to complete the study.
* 23\. Allergy to psilocybin, Microcrystalline Cellulose (MCC), or Niacin.
